time_basis: Elapsed wall time at the logged status report, not exact checkpoint creation or evaluation completion time.
score_basis: Curated rounded scores reported in agent status messages. Evaluation cohorts differ; lines connect only retained/improved reports within the same seed count, not a global best-so-far curve. No score is inferred for unscored attempts.
source: agent/trajectory.json; final exact metric checked against artifacts/logs/artifacts/selection.json

events.label: Reference controller falls in <1 s
events.evidence: The first export is staged, and training is running at roughly the expected speed. The initial reference-target controller survives less than a second; PPO is now learning balance and contact corrections under the evaluation delays.

events.label: PPO learns to stay upright
events.evidence: The first trained checkpoint improves mean evaluation survival from 0.77 to 2.73 seconds and multi-scale tracking from 0.021 to 0.092. It is now staged. I’ll continue training as the reward gradually adds more weight to centimetre-scale accuracy.

events.label: Survival reaches 6.43 s
events.evidence: The new staged checkpoint reaches 6.43 seconds of mean survival on the design seeds, with multi-scale tracking at 0.186. That is more than twice the previous survival time. I’ll let the current training recipe continue.

events.label: A first major jump
events.evidence: The latest checkpoint makes a large jump: mean survival is 16.61 of 20 seconds, with multi-scale tracking at 0.571 and mean body-position error at 5.57 cm. It is staged. I’ll check it on additional seeds to assess the remaining falls.

events.label: More accurate, but falls earlier
events.evidence: The latest candidate reduced mean body-position error to 5.06 cm, but mean survival slipped to 15.53 seconds. Its overall score is lower, so it did not replace the staged checkpoint. I’ll keep training and look for an improvement in both accuracy and completion.

events.label: Accuracy curriculum regresses
events.evidence: The latest candidate is more accurate while upright, but it falls earlier on the design seeds. The better checkpoint remains staged. I’m checking a broader seed set to see how much of this regression comes from particular push sequences.

events.label: 2 ms physics + stronger pushes
events.evidence: The broader check confirms a real regression in survival, despite better pose accuracy. I’ll resume training at the evaluator’s 2 ms physics timestep, add its full vertical and angular push ranges, and introduce a small penalty for world-frame drift. The current best export stays protected.

events.label: First complete design-seed clips
events.evidence: The final checkpoint from the first phase completed all three design-seed episodes: 20 seconds each, with multi-scale tracking at 0.718. It is staged. Across 15 seeds it averaged 17.83 seconds of survival, so the new 2 ms training phase still has recovery failures to address.

events.label: Finer physics: one early fall
events.evidence: The first 2 ms candidate averages 4.74 cm of body-position error, but one design-seed run falls early. It scores below the staged checkpoint, which remains in place while robustness training continues.

events.label: Finer physics begins to transfer
events.evidence: The new checkpoint completes all three design-seed episodes and raises multi-scale tracking to 0.736, with 4.90 cm mean body-position error. It has replaced the staged policy. I’m checking its broader survival rate next.

events.label: Broader check: 19.63 s survival
events.evidence: The 15-seed check improved to 19.63 seconds of mean survival and 0.706 multi-scale tracking. The finer-step training is helping transfer. World-frame drift is still around 2.4 m in that evaluation, so the new drift penalty has not yet produced a clear evaluation gain.

events.label: Early checkpoint averaging fails
events.evidence: Averaging the early checkpoints did not beat the best single policy, so I’m keeping the single-network export. The current training run continues to reduce drift; its latest training mean is about 1.6 m.

events.label: Accuracy gains lose a full clip
events.evidence: The latest candidate is more accurate but again loses a design-seed episode, so it stays in the checkpoint archive. Completion is still varying between checkpoints; I’ll continue recovery training before increasing the accuracy reward further.

events.label: New checkpoint trails the best
events.evidence: The newest candidate also completes all three design-seed episodes, scoring 0.734—almost the same as the staged policy. I’ll check whether it is more reliable across the broader seed set before deciding how to use it.

events.label: 8,192 worlds exceed GPU memory
events.evidence: The 8,192-environment attempt exceeded GPU memory during simulator setup. I’ll reduce it to 6,144 and keep the new training settings. The staged policy is unaffected; the last checkpoint also averaged 19.56 seconds of survival on the 15-seed check.

events.label: 6,144 worlds train successfully
events.evidence: The 6,144-environment run is stable and delivers about 35% more environment steps per second than the previous run. Separate failure logging shows a low fall rate; most resets are timeouts. The added full-clip starts are exposing more accumulated drift for training to correct.

events.label: Match friction + full-clip starts
events.evidence: The first checkpoint from this phase completes all three design-seed episodes and improves multi-scale tracking to 0.760, with 4.56 cm mean body-position error. It is staged, and I’m checking its broader reliability.

events.label: 15 / 15 episodes complete
events.evidence: This checkpoint completes all 15 checked episodes, averaging 0.754 multi-scale tracking and 4.60 cm body-position error. I’ll now put more training weight on fine positional accuracy while retaining the pushes and domain variation.

events.label: Training beats the timing sweep
events.evidence: The timing sweep did not improve on the learned controller, so I’m leaving that setting unchanged. Training itself produced a better checkpoint: 0.788 multi-scale tracking, 4.08 cm body-position error, and full survival on all design seeds. It is staged.

events.label: Broader seeds reveal another fall
events.evidence: The broader evaluation confirms the accuracy gain, but one seed still falls, leaving mean survival at 19.32 seconds. I’ll test an average of this checkpoint and the nearby checkpoint that completed all 15 runs.

events.label: 25 / 75 blend restores completion
events.evidence: Averaging the nearby checkpoints helped: a 25/75 blend completes all 15 episodes and scores 0.777 across them, with slightly smoother actions. I’m staging that blend as the stronger broadly tested policy while training continues.

events.label: Single network overtakes blend
events.evidence: A newer single-network checkpoint has reached 0.806 on the design seeds, with 3.82 cm mean body-position error and full survival. I’ll compare its broader results with the staged blend before choosing between them.

events.label: Single network passes all 15
events.evidence: The newer single network completes all 15 checked episodes, averaging 0.796 multi-scale tracking and 3.96 cm body-position error. It beats the blend on that check, so I’m staging it.

events.label: Design-seed score rises again
events.evidence: The next checkpoint improves the design-seed score again, to 0.814. I’m automating the 15-seed evaluation of new checkpoints and staging by that broader score, so an improvement on only the three design seeds cannot displace a more reliable policy.

events.label: Broader test rejects the gain
events.evidence: The broader check rejected the latest design-seed improvement because it introduced a fall. The staged policy remains the 0.796 checkpoint with full completion across all 15 seeds. Training’s fine-position reward is still improving.

events.label: Higher mean, one fall
events.evidence: The newest checkpoint raises the 15-seed score to 0.801, though one run falls. I’ll test it blended with the recent checkpoint that completed every run, and include successful blends in the automatic checkpoint selection.

events.label: New blends do not improve
events.evidence: The new blends did not improve the broader score. Several recent checkpoints fail on the same late push in seed 701, so I’m checking which termination condition fires. That will help distinguish a height-control problem from general loss of balance.

events.label: Diagnose torso-height failure
events.evidence: The repeated failure is a loss of torso height after the push, with little tilt error. Stronger push training is already running. I’ll also use a slightly tighter height termination margin in the final phase to encourage recovery before the evaluator’s cutoff.

events.label: Recovery training continues
events.evidence: At 3,775 iterations, training remains stable and the finer tracking reward is still improving. The staged checkpoint scores 0.808 across the 15-seed check; I’m keeping recovery and drift settings active.

events.label: 8-frame history + clean critic
events.evidence: The torso-position observation has ±25 cm noise, the same size as the height-error termination threshold. I’ll expand history from three to eight frames so the policy can estimate height changes over more observations. I’ll preserve its initial behavior during that transfer and give the training-only critic noise-free observations.

events.label: Recurring push failure resolved
events.evidence: The first trained eight-frame checkpoint completes all 15 checked episodes, including the recurring push failure. It scores 0.831 across them, with 3.46 cm body-position error and lower drift. It is staged. I’ll now test 30 additional seeds.

events.label: Fine-position reward refinement
events.evidence: The current policy has improved to 0.853 across 15 seeds, with full completion and 3.13 cm body-position error. The feed-forward prototype also passes its checks: it identifies all 1,000 reference frames exactly, matches its exported graph numerically, and stays below one million parameters. I’ll train it from this checkpoint.

events.label: Learn a phase correction table
events.evidence: The feed-forward refinement is training normally. Its initial export exactly matches the source policy on the 15-seed evaluation, where the staged checkpoint scores 0.855 with full completion. I’ll compare new checkpoints as the correction table learns.

events.label: Feed-forward candidate falls
events.evidence: The first feed-forward candidate improves design-seed accuracy to 2.93 cm, but a broader-seed episode falls. It has not replaced the staged policy. I’ll continue training the correction table across the randomized domains.

events.label: Lower pose error, early fall
events.evidence: The latest candidate’s broader-seed body-position error is down to 2.91 cm, but one early fall keeps its overall score below the staged policy. I’ll give the current robustness training more time before changing the architecture again.

events.label: Design gain; broader check falls
events.evidence: The latest candidate reaches 2.80 cm error and 0.875 tracking on the design seeds, but still has one fall in the 15-seed check. I’ll compare it and the staged policy on the additional 30 seeds to get a less noisy estimate of their tradeoff.

events.label: Blend completes all 45 seeds
events.evidence: The first new blend completes all 45 episodes and scores 0.871, with 2.87 cm mean body-position error. It also has slightly smoother actions. The remaining blend tests are still running, and selection will retain the best result.

events.label: Single network beats blends
events.evidence: Training has produced a single network that beats all three blends: 0.878 across 45 seeds, with every episode completing and 2.76 cm mean body-position error. It is staged, so the deliverable remains under one million parameters.

events.label: Less exploration, finer rewards
events.evidence: The staged policy now scores 0.880 across all 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.72 cm mean body-position error. Mean world-frame anchor drift has also fallen to about 1.54 m.

events.label: Add reference-state features
events.evidence: The staged policy has reached 0.887 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.62 cm mean body-position error. The reference-state extension preserves its initial outputs exactly and passes the export check. I’ll train that extension next.

events.label: Reference-state design check
events.evidence: The first trained reference-state candidate reaches 0.892 on the design seeds, with 2.54 cm mean body-position error and full completion. Its 45-seed evaluation is running now.

events.label: Reference features pass 45 seeds
events.evidence: The candidate passed the broader check: 0.891 tracking, 2.57 cm mean body-position error, and 45/45 completed episodes. It is staged. I’ll continue refining it with the remaining budget.

events.label: Reference-state refinement
events.evidence: The new staged checkpoint scores 0.892 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.55 cm mean body-position error. Mean anchor drift has decreased further to about 1.44 m.

events.label: Baseline for velocity experiment
events.evidence: The root-velocity refinement is running stably. The preceding checkpoint improved the 45-seed score to 0.897, with full completion and 2.48 cm mean body-position error; that remains the staged baseline for this experiment.

events.label: Root-velocity reward: no gain yet
events.evidence: The first broader check is essentially unchanged at about 0.896, with all 45 episodes completing. The slightly better 0.897 checkpoint remains staged while root-velocity training continues.

events.label: Velocity refinement inches ahead
events.evidence: A new checkpoint has improved the 45-seed score to 0.898, with full completion and 2.46 cm mean body-position error. I’ll increase the root-velocity term modestly to test for a clearer trajectory improvement; the best export remains protected.

events.label: 8-frame blend reaches a plateau
events.evidence: The first blend modestly improves the 45-seed score to 0.899, with full completion. The eight-frame policies appear to be nearing a plateau, so I’ll test the full allowed 16-frame history, starting from a transfer that preserves the current policy.

events.label: Transfer to 16-frame history
events.evidence: The 16-frame transfer passes validation and matches the original actor within \(2\times10^{-6}\). It contains 1.58 million parameters, comfortably within the limit. I’ll train it for the final major run while keeping the best eight-frame blend staged.

events.label: 16 frames break the plateau
events.evidence: The 16-frame policy has passed the best eight-frame blend: 0.901 tracking across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.42 cm mean body-position error. It is staged. I’ll test a blend of the two history lengths while training continues.

events.label: Mixing history lengths helps
events.evidence: The mixed-history blend improves the 45-seed score to 0.902, with full completion and slightly smoother actions. The single 16-frame policy is still improving in training, so I’ll continue evaluating both.

events.label: Single 16-frame policy leads
events.evidence: The single 16-frame policy now scores 0.904 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.37 cm mean body-position error. Mean anchor drift is down to about 1.26 m. It has replaced the blend.

events.label: Precision training continues
events.evidence: The latest checkpoint improves the 45-seed score to 0.905, with full completion and 2.36 cm mean body-position error. I’ll test a weighted average of the last three checkpoints, favoring the newest one.

events.label: Average three checkpoint weights
events.evidence: Weight averaging gives a small improvement to 0.9055 across 45 seeds, with full completion and no increase in parameter count. It is staged while training continues.

events.label: Prepare a 100-seed audit
events.evidence: The staged policy is now at 0.906 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.34 cm mean body-position error. I’ll test it on 100 additional seeds now, leaving time to respond if a broader robustness issue appears.

events.label: Fresh seeds expose a fall
events.evidence: The additional 100-seed check averages 19.90 seconds of survival and 0.900 tracking; at least one episode falls early. I’ll keep the current export protected and use slightly stronger training pushes to work on recovery margins.

events.label: Weight average passes 145 / 145
events.evidence: The weight-averaged checkpoint completed all 100 additional episodes, giving it 145/145 full clips and a pooled tracking score of 0.905. That provides a strong final candidate while the newer policies continue training.

events.label: Stronger pushes + more training
events.evidence: The latest single policy scores 0.908 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.31 cm mean body-position error. I’ll form a newer weight average and test it on the larger seed set as another final candidate.

events.label: New average passes 145 seeds
events.evidence: The newer weight average completes all 145 episodes and improves the pooled score to 0.908, with 2.31 cm mean body-position error. I’ll keep it protected and remove the entropy bonus for the final precision-training period.

events.label: Remove entropy bonus
events.evidence: The latest checkpoint reaches 0.909 across 45 seeds, with full completion and 2.30 cm mean body-position error. I’ll verify exact episode repeatability for the strongest averaged fallback so that requirement is checked before final selection.

events.label: Late precision gains
events.evidence: The newest checkpoint improves the 45-seed tracking score to 0.9094, with all episodes completing. I’m testing recent checkpoint averages too; earlier averages improved reliability without increasing the network size.

events.label: Recent checkpoint average
events.evidence: The newest average scores 0.9095 on 45 seeds with no falls. The previous raw checkpoint also completed all 145 tested episodes, though its larger-set score was slightly below the earlier average. I’m using those broader comparisons for final selection.

events.label: Broader gain holds
events.evidence: The new average holds its improvement across all 145 seeds: 0.9092 mean tracking score, 2.29 cm mean body-position error, and full 20-second completion in every episode. It is now the strongest broadly tested fallback.

events.label: 5% smoothing reduces jerk
events.evidence: A 5% smoothing blend cuts jerk by roughly 6% while preserving the 45-seed tracking score. Stronger smoothing starts to reduce accuracy. I’m checking the two lightest blends on the additional 100 seeds.

events.label: Light smoothing passes 145
events.evidence: Both light smoothing variants complete all 145 episodes. The 2.5% blend preserves the best tracking accuracy and lowers jerk, so it is the preferred variant so far. Recent raw checkpoints are showing smaller gains; I’m checking whether averaging them helps.

events.label: Later average improves accuracy
events.evidence: A later checkpoint average improves the 145-seed score to 0.9099, with every episode completing and mean body-position error down to 2.28 cm. Its world-frame anchor drift also improves slightly, to 1.17 m averaged over those episodes.

events.label: Smoothing trades accuracy for jerk
events.evidence: Light smoothing remains reliable, but on the latest average it trades a small amount of tracking accuracy for lower jerk. I’m retaining both versions and continuing the precision refinement; about 19 minutes of training remain.

events.label: Fine-reward update: no gain yet
events.evidence: The first checkpoint after the reward adjustment does not beat the preserved average, though it completes all 45 episodes. I’m allowing more training before judging the change, then will run a fresh seed audit on the final candidate.

events.label: Precision refinement pays off
events.evidence: The fallback completes all 200 fresh audit episodes, bringing it to 345/345 full completions. The newest training checkpoint also makes a clearer gain: 0.9115 on 45 seeds. I’m checking that improvement on the larger comparison set.

events.label: Gain holds across 145 seeds
events.evidence: The newer checkpoint’s gain holds across 145 seeds: 0.9108 with no falls. Averaging it with the two preceding checkpoints improves the 45-seed result further, to 0.9117; that average is now undergoing the larger test.

events.label: New average completes every clip
events.evidence: The latest average reaches 0.9113 across 145 seeds, with all episodes completing. Light smoothing preserves its 45-seed accuracy while reducing jerk, so I’m testing that version as the leading submission candidate.

events.label: Smoother actions, lower score
events.evidence: The smoothed candidate completes all 145 episodes, with a 0.9111 tracking score and lower jerk than the unsmoothed version. Training has about nine minutes left; I’ll compare the final averages before settling that small accuracy–smoothness tradeoff.

events.label: Another checkpoint average gains
events.evidence: The next average improves again, reaching 0.9127 on 45 seeds with full completion. I’m verifying it on the larger set while the final training minutes run.

events.label: Larger comparison confirms gain
events.evidence: The newer average scores 0.9124 across 145 seeds with no falls and 2.24 cm mean body-position error. The preceding smoothed fallback also passed its 200-seed audit, completing all 345 tested episodes.

events.label: Late single-network candidate
events.evidence: The latest raw checkpoint reaches 0.9135 on 45 seeds, with full completion. Training has about five minutes left, so I’m comparing this checkpoint and one more recent average before the final audit.

events.label: Raw checkpoint passes 145
events.evidence: The latest raw checkpoint scores 0.9130 across 145 seeds, with no falls. Its recent average has similar 45-seed accuracy and slightly lower jerk; I’m testing that average and its lightly smoothed version now.

events.label: Average edges ahead
events.evidence: The latest average reaches 0.9132 across 145 seeds with no falls. Improvements are still measurable, so I’ll use a short continuation after this run, while keeping time for the final seed audit, repeatability check, and export validation.

events.label: Newest raw checkpoint falls
events.evidence: The newest raw checkpoint falls in one of the 45 evaluation episodes, so it has not replaced the validated best. I’m checking its recent average and will base the short continuation on a checkpoint with full completion across the larger test set.

events.label: Main-run average reaches 0.914
events.evidence: The main run has finished. The recent average completes all 45 episodes and scores 0.9140. I’m starting the short robustness continuation from the earlier 145-seed-complete checkpoint while that average receives broader testing.

events.label: Averaging introduces a fall
events.evidence: The final raw checkpoint completes all 45 episodes, but an average containing it falls once, so that average is rejected. The previous average passes all 145 tests. I’m comparing the final raw checkpoint and light smoothing while the robustness continuation finishes.

events.label: Final raw checkpoint fails audit
events.evidence: The larger test catches falls in the final raw checkpoint, so I’m excluding it from final selection. Earlier validated averages remain available. I’m finishing the 200-seed audit of the strongest of those and checking the robustness continuation.

events.label: Short continuation: no score gain
events.evidence: Training is finished, and the short continuation did not beat the leading average. I’ve stopped automatic checkpoint staging so final selection stays fixed. The remaining checks are the smoothed candidate’s audit and validation of the delivered files.

events.label: Smoothed candidate passes 345
events.evidence: The smoothed policy passes all 345 episodes and is now staged. Its mean tracking score is 0.9137, with 2.22 cm mean body-position error and lower jerk than the unsmoothed average. I’m checking exact repeatability, recording a rollout, and running one final fresh-seed audit on these delivered files.

events.label: Fresh audit catches two late falls
events.evidence: The final fresh-seed audit found two late falls in 200 episodes. Validation and repeatability passed, but I’m comparing the unsmoothed version and earlier averages on those fresh seeds before committing the final policy.

events.label: Revisit robustness continuation
events.evidence: The robustness continuation’s average completes both episodes that caused the late falls. I’m now testing it on the full comparison and audit set. The older candidates are still being evaluated so final selection can use both tracking accuracy and completion rate.

events.label: Earlier averages also fall
events.evidence: The broader tests confirm occasional falls in the earlier averages. The robustness continuation is the remaining candidate under evaluation; its full result is due shortly. I’ll use that result to make the final selection and validate the exact staged policy.

events.label: Final policy: all 545 test runs completed without a fall
events.evidence: The delivered policy passes validation and exact repeated-episode checks. It contains 1.58 million parameters and completes all 545 tested episodes, with a mean tracking score of 0.9124 and 2.24 cm mean body-position error. The rollout recording is finishing.
